name: fastify
extractedFrom: Newly created — a scratch reference implementation (Fastify 5.12.7 · drizzle-orm 0.45.4 · embedded PostgreSQL 18.4) was built and run first, and its files were then moved into the fences. No other pack was opened, not even as a format reference (only assets/pack-resource-template.md was used)
policyEngineNote: There is no row-level policy engine. The application connects to the DB over a trusted connection, so **a missing ownership filter is a data leak outright**. On top of that this axis has a second trap, **plugin encapsulation** — set the auth hook on a sibling plugin and it does not reach the routes, so a 200 goes out without auth (confirmed by running it). Carrying the BaaS axis's 'RLS is the backup, so the application check is defense in depth' narrative over to this axis produces exactly the opposite instruction — a value that must be passed on when generating the seam

exampleDomain.note: Every pack and seam uses the same example domain. L0 issues the vocabulary policy (`vocab-task`) from these values and the gate blocks any divergence

fixesVariantsNote: The handler shape (Fastify 5 plugin encapsulation · route schema · type provider) and the query shape (the Drizzle query builder + drizzle-kit migrations) are the premise of the entire pack body. For a project that picked Express, backend/node-api owns that shape; for NestJS, backend/node-nest; for the Hono + AWS turnkey stack, backend/aws-container. A project using Prisma with Fastify would get wrong instructions from this pack — that is the generation path
pkgsNote: vitest is pinned to 3 — 5.0.4 (vite 8 · rolldown) failed at startup because an npm optional-dependency defect left it unable to find its native binding (measured 2026-10-15). The fastify-plugin 6 line (6.0.0 = 2026-06-09, 6.0.1 = 2026-10-10) has not been verified in combination with Fastify 5 — pinned to 5. pino is owned by fastify (10.x) — the pack's code never imports pino directly. jose@6 · @fastify/cookie@11 · @fastify/cors@11 came in with the auth variants in 3.35.0 (2026-10-17 npm latest 6.2.12 · 11.1.3 · 11.3.1; both plugins' devDependencies are fastify ^5.0.0 — execution not verified). @fastify/rate-limit@11 also came in with the self-issued variant in 3.35.0 (2026-10-17 npm latest 11.2.1, devDependencies fastify ^5.0.0, no peerDependencies — only the per-route 429 and reaching errorHandler were observed running in the scratch; the pack code gets only the pack-smoke typecheck). The three plugins use fastify-plugin 6 as an internal dependency, but the pack code's fp import stays pinned to 5. Only the self-issued variant imports @fastify/cookie. Password hashing is node:crypto scrypt, so there is no package (removes the native-binding failure path)
runtimeNote: These are server runtime versions, not npm dependencies. Put them in pkgs and `npm i` fetches the wrong package. The reference implementation ran on PostgreSQL 18.4 (embedded-postgres) and Node 24.7 — the SQL and features the pack uses are the same from 16 up

clusters.why: The shape of the validation error a route schema throws (err.validation · validationContext) and fieldErrors, which turns it into field errors, are functions of each other. Both files know that unknown keys arrive with instancePath '/'

Ownership of the db singleton and the wiring in buildApp are the same decision (it stays a module rather than being carried as a decorator). The layering discipline 'the data layer knows nothing about HTTP' also spans both files

They share the process lifetime (boot · shutdown · pool · health checks). Close the pool in onClose and tests break when they build the app several times — the two files see the same decision from opposite sides

clustersNote: This was serial authoring that built the reference implementation first, so the clusters were not used as units of parallel work (the same approach as node-nest). They are kept as a record of the coupling — when repairing, look at both files of the same cluster together

knownGaps.what: propagating the request correlation ID to downstream calls
knownGaps.detail: We confirmed only that Fastify puts req.id on req.log. The AsyncLocalStorage wiring that passes that ID on to external HTTP calls and queues was not run, so it was left empty — 'an empty slot beats wrong content'

The basis for the instruction 'run migrations once, as a step separate from the deploy' is principle, not observation. There is no measurement of running drizzle-kit migrate from two processes at once
npm latest is 7.0.2, but we pinned typescript@5. The other packs and the pack-smoke profile assume 5, and this pack's tsconfig (moduleResolution bundler) was not run on 7

Only the four FST_ERR_CTP_* codes we observed are mapped. Other request-stage 4xx errors, such as a bad Content-Length or URL encoding, fall through toAppError to a 500 INTERNAL — we could not enumerate them by running (raised by audit C)

Execution is pinned to tsx (development and production alike, boot confirmed by running). Because of top-level await and extensionless imports, the tsc output cannot be run directly with node, and the bundling path is not covered (raised by audit C)

knownGaps.what: execution verification of the slots absorbed in 3.35.0
knownGaps.detail: api-endpoints · complete-example · the two auth variants were written without being run (pack-smoke not run). The <!-- unverified --> tag in each file states the scope. The existing 6 files' tests were also not re-run after the envelope changed to { data }

knownGaps.what: grace window for concurrent refresh requests
knownGaps.detail: When two requests arrive at once with the same refresh token (two tabs), the second is judged a reuse and the family is cut. No grace window allowing the previous token for a few seconds was added — the safe-side default
Whether './src/db/*schema.ts' reads schema.ts and auth-schema.ts together was not run. If it does not, write it as an array

The default store of @fastify/rate-limit is process memory. With several instances a Redis store is needed, but none was attached and run. An account (email) key limit was not added either — IP key only

variantsNote: Only the auth method is a variant. Both variants ship auth-boundaries.md (the boundary: environment keys · requireAuth · AuthUser · authFor) and auth-flows.md (the flow: authPlugin — for self-issued, the /api/auth routes · cookies · CORS; for OIDC, CORS and the IdP registration items) under the same names. The installer copies the chosen directory's files into resources/
seamSlotsNote: In 3.35.0 the pack absorbed the three slots api-endpoints · auth-boundaries · complete-example — the wire contract (http-standard@1) became the single authority, so the envelope is no longer a function of the combination, and the remaining variable (the auth method) is handled by variants.auth
